Every time a couple has an offspring, the offspring has an equal chance of inheriting each of the probable traitsFor a single allele, all offspring will have a 25%chance of inheriting any genotype.Probability of a dominant phenotype 75% or 3:1For a dihybrid cross, 1:16 chance of each combination of alleles. For dominance, ratio is always 9:3:3:1 for traits with autosomal dominance/recessive
explanation: For each fertilization event, the offspring has an equal chance of inheriting any of the possible parental alleles. In a monohybrid cross of two heterozygotes, there is a 25% (1/4) chance for each genotype (e.g., EE, Ee, eE, ee), resulting in a 75% (3/4) probability of expressing the dominant phenotype, which represents the classic 3:1 ratio. In a dihybrid cross, there is a 1/16 chance for each specific combination of alleles, leading to a classic 9:3:3:1 phenotypic ratio for traits that exhibit standard autosomal dominant/recessive inheritance.
